rites.name: Soria
rites.text: Soria is the concept of resonance that rang through Eluannys during the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed out of sound. It is less a being than a pattern of tones that binds matter wherever it echoes.

rites.name: Kraigak
rites.text: Kraigak is the concept of the Stillness-Before-Song in Eluannys, the held breath that the first roots of the world used to condense out of resonance. Temples of the Holy Age preserve its name in flame and hymn, treating it as the grammar by which all later matter was spoken into being.

rites.name: Corallistia
rites.text: A grappling technique in which a fighter catches an opponent's limb and turns the attacker's own rush against them, hurling them onto the ground. The fighter may roll sideways to add force to the throw.

rites.name: Rosanum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver where a fighter slips behind a rival, tucks the head beneath the rival's shoulder, hoists them up, and drives them down tailbone-first across a raised knee.

rites.name: Rilia
rites.text: A combatant charges at a rival and sweeps one outstretched arm across the throat or chest, knocking the foe flat. Observers often mistake it for a similar strike called a lariat.

rites.name: Orillanum Maunor
rites.text: A grappling restraint applied from behind, where one arm bends the foe's limb across their face while the free arm locks the hold closed. It forces the captive to yield or fall senseless by pressing on the neck.

rites.name: Tesantanum
rites.text: A holding craft that bends a fighter's elbow or shoulder past its natural range to force a surrender. It works best while both bodies are pressed to the ground, and when pushed too hard it can tear sinew or snap bone.

rites.name: Saurniastum
rites.text: A fighter seizes a rival's skull and leaps forward, dropping down so the rival's face is slammed into the ground. Related variations of this takedown are sometimes called face-smashers.

rites.name: Leolia
rites.text: A fighter falls backward while gripping a foe's head, slamming the skull into the ground. Some combatants prefix it with a stomach strike to lower the target's head first.

rites.name: Celarnus
rites.text: Celarnus is a concept of the Arcane Realm within Eluannys, bound to the memory of the Fall and the Sundering, when worlds broke apart and the Pact was sworn in the groves. It is remembered as the thread that held the shards of broken worlds together through the early age of the first sovereign.

rites.name: Drogurkun
rites.text: Drogurkun is the concept of the Pact that was sworn in the Fall, when the Sundering broke worlds into Shards and the first sovereign bound the surviving groves to one oath. It is remembered in the Age of growing kingdoms as the principle that a broken thing may still be mended by shared promise.

rites.name: Fenode
rites.text: Fenode is a concept of Eluannys, a sealed fire-thread drawn from the Fall, when the Sundering split the worlds into Shards. Its flame was bound by the Pact during the Holy Age, and temples still keep it burning in cold vessels.

rites.name: Viallium
rites.text: A fighter climbs high onto a post, then leaps forward and spins through a turn and a half in the air. The spin ends with the fighter crashing down flat across a rival lying in the ring.

rites.name: Mestor Laror
rites.text: A spinning double-footed strike aimed at a foe draped over the ropes, grabbing the cords mid-turn. Fighters use it to set up a bigger throw rather than to end the bout.

rites.name: Viarnia
rites.text: A grappling technique in which the attacker stretches an opponent's frame while risking a count-out. It is usually used early in a contest or as a lead-in to a stronger hold.

rites.name: Rolus
rites.text: A grappling maneuver in which a fighter lifts an opponent upside down and drops them into a throw, a variant developed by a notable wrestler who blends a flip with a sharp chop-like dump.

rites.name: Reorus
rites.text: A combat technique in which a fighter lifts a foe onto their shoulders, cradles the neck and a leg, then sinks to the ground so the opponent crashes headfirst into the floor. A rarer throat-cutting variant also exists.

rites.name: Sallia
rites.text: A combat technique in which one fighter lifts an opponent and drops them with a sharp twist, while a partner's help adds force to the throw.

rites.name: Raseontus
rites.text: A coordinated maneuver in which allies lift a foe into place so that a third party can slam their face down. One attacker supports the victim in a wheelbarrow stance while companions complete the strike from there.

rites.name: Amolanum
rites.text: A tumbling maneuver in which one fighter hurls a partner off a raised platform so the partner lands in a leap onto a rival waiting nearby. It is often used by a common acrobat of the arena.

rites.name: Oresiarium
rites.text: A grappling technique in which a fighter lifts an opponent and drives them head-first into the ground while facing away. It is a twisted form of a related drop that looks more dangerous than the forbidden holds.

rites.name: Valiarnor
rites.text: A grappling hold in which a fighter seizes a rival around the middle, lifts them clear of the ground, and crushes their back and ribs. Some fighters skip the lift and simply squeeze and shake the foe instead.

rites.name: Nireonum
rites.text: A rarely used grappling hold in which a fighter stands atop a rival's back and pulls sharply on both arms. It was once the signature technique of a famed brawler and is now occasionally used as a backup finishing move.

rites.name: Leoliastus
rites.text: A grappling throw where a fighter seizes a rival by the throat, hoists them aloft, and drives them down onto the floor. It looks fearsome yet is considered fairly safe, and tougher fighters often use it to finish a bout.

rites.name: Siarus
rites.text: A grappling maneuver where a fighter hooks a foe's leg in a crook of the arm, lifts them upside down, and drops to a knee so the head strikes the ground. A variant tucks one arm between the foe's legs and drives them down headfirst.

rites.name: Calaunes
rites.text: A leaping strike performed by standing on one leg with arms raised like a bird's wings, then kicking an opponent in the chest. Some fighters use it as a signature finishing blow.

rites.name: Meneosor
rites.text: A bound-arm lift in which a fighter locks a bent foe's limbs across the body, hoists them upright, and drives them down between the fighter's own legs. It is a crushing finishing maneuver used in close combat.

rites.name: Rises
rites.text: A fighter charges at a rival and smashes an elbow-bent forearm into the head or neck. It differs from a straight-armed blow, and a famous brawler is said to have first used it.

rites.name: Amaurasanum
rites.text: A grappling hold in which an opponent's legs are bound while their arms are locked behind them and pulled. Many later fighters adopted it after its first famous user.

rites.name: Thiasith
rites.text: Thiasith is a concept of Eluannys, the practice of building and keeping walls that hold back the wild while letting certain doors open. Through the centuries of the Walled Age it bound orders, churches and first crossings together, shaping how the groves and growing kingdoms of the first sovereign learned to live with boundaries.

rites.name: Tonium
rites.text: Tonium is the concept of resonant binding in Eluannys, the force that holds walls, orders and churches together across the Walled Age. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds, Tonium was the thread that kept first crossings from unravelling.

rites.name: Vollaurum
rites.text: A paired maneuver in which one fighter hoists a foe skyward while the partner catches the foe's head in a tight hold. A later team adopted it under a shortened brand that means finishing the job at once.

rites.name: Neollum
rites.text: A high-flying aerial maneuver performed from the top rope, where the performer launches into a flip spinning three and a half turns before landing a body slam. It was spread across a southern region by a daring acrobat.

rites.name: Lenaustum
rites.text: A chant-like ritual melody that a champion of the arena first claims as the sound announcing their entrance. It marks the moment a fighter steps forth into the crowd's gaze.

rites.name: Orolia
rites.text: A daring aerial leap where a fighter springs backward off a board and flips over to strike below. It is performed from a high rope for extra balance and ranks above simpler dives.

rites.name: Collor
rites.text: A fighter seizes an rival's wrist and wrenches the arm, then climbs the corner posts and strides along the topmost cord before leaping down to strike the foe's chest or neck.

rites.name: Valiasirnum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver that a veteran fighter uses to end matches, resembling a spinning reversal strike but performed without any support from the boundary cords of the ring.

rites.name: Oronarium
rites.text: A fighter seats a rival in a corner, leaps onto the rival's chest, and bounces there. The crowd usually treats it as a bit of comedy rather than a real injury.

rites.name: Vosaullor
rites.text: A signature kick performed by a masked fighter in a sporting arena. It is a rare technique, not commonly used by the local combatants of its region.

rites.name: Orantestor
rites.text: A fighter hoists a rival onto a corner post, then bounds from the rigging before dropping down onto them in a seated fall. One warrior claims this maneuver as a personal trademark and calls it the Tear Drop.

rites.name: Naunteorum
rites.text: A grappling hold that forces a foe's head and neck into a clamp while pulling back the arms. It is a favored finishing technique among fighters, and a few rivals have adopted it in later bouts.

rites.name: Valeostum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver where a fighter hoists a rival onto the shoulders, pins both arms in a cross, and drops to the knees so the rival crashes onto the floor. Several champions have adopted it as their decisive closing technique.

rites.name: Raulus Centolium
rites.text: A grappling maneuver where a fighter locks an opponent's head under one arm, then falls backward to slam their face into the floor. Its sharp drop inspired a seated variant used to strike the jaw across the shoulder.

rites.name: Teliasirnum
rites.text: A bodily discipline devised by a former fighter after a crippling injury forced him out of his career. It blends gentle stretching with strength work to help people recover and stay fit.

rites.name: Rales Amiserium
rites.text: A somber chant sung by a grim keeper of the arena. It was carried into the bouts for a stretch of time before the keeper changed to a different hymn.
